note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (committed; problem_index, attempt, n_new, cap_hit, score_v3) and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (problems: index, level, base_k). Filters: attempt == 0, pool problems with base_k in {1,2,3} and level in {1,2,3}, cap-hit rows dropped, right = score_v3 == 1, finished-wrong = score_v3 == 0. Per problem the mean of ln(n_new / median right n_new), then the median over problems (numpy median, so an even count averages the two middle values). alt_measured = median of the pooled per-row r_i across all finished-wrong rows (row-weighted instead of problem-weighted). base_k is taken from the pool file as written (per its 'what' field it comes from the same job's attempt-0 rows under grader v3; not cross-checked against rows.jsonl); a problem whose only wrong rows are cap hits drops out. n_new is >= 74 in every row, so no log of zero. Levels 1-3 hold only 65 pool problems, fewer after the right-and-wrong requirement, so the median rests on a small sample.

Same files and code as p1 with level == 5 only (78 pool problems at level 5 before the right/finished-wrong requirement). alt_measured = median of the pooled per-row r_i. On Level 5 many wrong samples are cap hits; these are dropped by the recipe, which removes the longest failures and pulls the statistic toward zero or below, so the number measures only finished wrong attempts.

Files as p1. Pooled over finished-wrong attempt-0 rows (cap hits dropped) of pool problems with base_k in {1,2,3}, level in {1,2,3} and at least one right attempt-0 row; hit = n_new strictly less than every right sibling's n_new (ties are not hits, as the recipe says). alt_measured = share of those rows strictly below the median n_new of the right siblings (the definition in the GPU prediction, the most likely other reading of 'shorter than right siblings'). The chance level depends on the number of right siblings (1-3), so the 0.35 threshold is not an exact null.

Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl and pool_k_le3.json (rl_k). Main reading, literal: problems in pool_k_le3 (only problems where the cued base has at most 3 of 4 right, 183 problems) with rl_k in {1,2,3}, any level (about 50 problems before the right-and-wrong requirement). alt_measured: the experiment text says 'RL plain, all levels', which could mean every MATH-500 problem where RL has 1-3 of 4 right, not just the base-hard pool; the alt recomputes rl_k from the RL attempt-0 rows (score_v3 == 1, cap hits not right) over all 500 problems and applies the same statistic. RL has few finished wrong samples (185 score-0 rows total, including cap hits and restarts), so the median rests on few problems.
